items.title: Kenny Barron — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: a call from the guy who was our manager – road manager, Billy Hoogstraten.

ctx.x: People Time is the name of it.

Yeah. We would end with that song, which I think was a Benny Carter composition. I’m not sure. I think it’s Benny Carter. But people started asking, “Why don’t you do . . .?” – “You two guys should do a duo recording.” So I guess he took it to heart. He hooked it up. We went back to the Montmartre, because we had recorded previously some radio broadcasts there that came out as recordings. Stan loved the sound so much – one was called Anniversary, and one was called Serenity, with the quartet. He loved the sound…
time I had started working with him, he had gotten over all his bad habits, substance abuse and drinking. He was fine, and he was a nice cat.
